heard: A dead star is slowly vaporizing its own companion into thin air. In 1988, astronomers discovered PSR B1957 plus 20, a rapidly spinning neutron star in our galaxy. It rotates once every 1.6 milliseconds, while its small companion completes a tight orbit every 9.2 hours. As the pulsar races through space at 1 million kilometers per hour, it generates a bright bow shock. The pulsar blasts this partner with radiation, stripping away its surface material until the star becomes nothing. Fermi data updated its mass to 1.8 solar masses, finally proving the star is a cold cosmic cannibal. This is exactly why you will find a dead star, is slowly vaporizing its own companion into thin air.
